First question is whether the facts have any significance. Second is what is the explanation. Answer to the first 
is that they don't. They have no scientific interest, and they tell us nothing about how to deal with Tom Jones — who is 
who is he, and not the mean of some group to which we assign him. 
As for explanation, the likelihood I think is what I outlined, say the likely different outcomes for a kid like me and 
a counterpart in a family in Philly that is part of a group that for 400 years had a chance for about 2 or 3 decades to 
enter mainstream society, and then with the constant legacy of miserable racism. There were a few families that 
escaped the legacy — Thurgood Marshall, Condoleezza Rice, etc. But it's not surprising under the circumstances that 
few did. And simply as a matter of biology, the capacities involved are so deeply embedded that it would be quite 
surprising if an evolutionarily brief period that has produced only superficial changes would have affected them. 
But in any event, I don't see the importance (except on ugly assumptions), any more than it would be important 
to show that tall people with blue eyes on average do better (or worse) in answering questions on tests. 
But for later discussion.

Google buys Deep Mind ... 
Wow, did you see this? 
http://recode.net/2014/01/26/exclusive-google-to-buy-artificial-intelligence-startup-deepmind-for-400m/ 
That is the company I often pointed out as being the most likely competitor to OpenCog in really pushing toward AGI... 
And I happen to know (from my friendship with their co-founder Shane Legg, who will now become a very wealthy 
Google employee) that Deep Mind has *nothing* technologically besides some interesting proto-AGI R&D code.... 
Nothing that works, really. 
So it's pretty much an acqui-hire .... And 50 programmers for $400M 
is a really fat acquihire; $1M - $2M per programmer is way more typical... this shows that Google values anything Al or 
robotics ish quite a lot these days... 
One read of the overall situation would be "Google is going to win the race to AGI" -- they have a lot of $5 and are 
looking to hire the entire Al and robotics field... Maybe they will change their name to CyberDyne systems (cf 
"Terminator" ...) 
OTOH, more money doesn't •always• win; having the right set of ideas also means a lot.... Linux, not Windows, 
dominates supercomputing and 
the Internet.... And they are not doing proto-AGI within Google X, 
they're doing it in their main product dev division, which brings a complicated set of compromises... Hmmm... 
Interesting times !!! 
more later...
